desc: Stress-test clause 4 on remaining uncovered (O,E,F) classes: (4,0,2) predicted L, (4,3,0) predicted W, (6,2,0) predicted L, (6,1,1) predicted L (E+F=2 even; enumerate: fill→(6,1,0)=W opp, oo→(4,2,1)=W opp, oe→(6,0,1)=W opp ⇒ L ✓), and (8,0,0) predicted L (oo→(6,1,0)=W only option ⇒ L ✓). Confirm each by one-ply enumeration against already-established base cases.

Write the final proof sketch: (i) N odd ⇒ A·B even ⇒ total-moves parity = M parity; (ii) N even, O=0 ⇒ all d_i even ⇒ A·B parity fixed; (iii) N even, O=2 ⇒ first player takes the decisive last-bit merge and sets parity; (iv) N even, O≥4 ⇒ last-bit-maker wins and the stall game reduces to "losing iff E+F even" with base cases (2,·) winning and (4, E+F even) losing, noting the mover's F-parity control on merges never changes the outcome classes.

Finalize and validate the O(N+M) code (already in CURRENT SOLUTION) against samples 1–3 and edge cases: N=1 (Takahashi), M=0 N=2 (Aoki), M=0 even N≥4 (Takahashi), single complete-bipartite component, N=2e5 performance.
Brute-force solver script written (bitmask state, memoized win/lose, clause testers for N≤5 exhaustive + N=6 ≤3-edge sweep + targeted families) — no execution environment available to run it.
Hand-verified base cases: isolated N=2→Aoki, N=4→Takahashi, N=6→Takahashi; (2,1)+(2,1)→Aoki; samples 1–3 all consistent with the 4-clause formula.
Established N-odd clause (A·B always even ⇒ L parity = M parity) and O=0 clause (all d_i even ⇒ A·B parity fixed) with solid algebra.

Parity-flip analysis of Φ=E+F under all move types: fills flip F; even-even merges preserve Φ; odd-odd merges preserve Φ-parity; odd-even merges give mover optional Φ-flip — base-case enumeration still consistent with clause 4.

Hand-enumerated decisive game trees: (4,0,0)=L, (4,0,1)=W, (4,1,0)=W, (4,1,1)=L, (4,2,0)=L, (4,2,1)=W, (6,0,0)=L, (6,1,0)=W, (6,0,1)=W; O=2 cases (2 iso + 2 edges, (2,1)+(2,1), N=2) all first-player wins — all consistent with the four-clause rule.
